gloss: end, edge, extremity; cut off; commander
summary: The end or edge of a thing: of a staff, a camp, a border, a curtain, and above all of the earth and the heavens, “from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth”. It marks the end of a span of time (“at the end of three days”), and “from the end” of a people is from its whole range, so in late books מִקְצָת is “some of”. The rare verb cuts off or cuts short, of peoples, feet and Israel's borders, and scrapes a wall; the Peshitta's ܩܨܐ of the same root breaks the bread. Arabic qaṣā, aqṣā “be far, farthest” and Aramaic קְצָת “end, part” share the sense of the outermost point; whether קָצִין “commander” belongs to the same older root is not settled.

words.summary: About ninety-five times, nearly always in construct or with מִן: the end or edge of a place, a thing, the earth or a time. The spelling קֵצֶה, in the phrase “there is no end”, is the same word.

senses.gloss: end, edge (of a place or thing)
senses.definition: The outer end or edge of something: a wilderness, a border, a camp, a curtain, a staff, a heap.

evidence.note: Etham “at the edge of the wilderness”.
The southern border runs “from the end of the Sea of Salt”.
The angel of Yahweh put out “the end of the staff” in his hand and touched the meat.
Jonathan dips “the end of the staff” in the honeycomb.
Kadesh, “a city at the edge of your border”.
Loops on the edge of the curtain.
Gideon goes down to the edge of the camp.
The lepers come to the edge of the camp of Aram.
Fire consumes at the edge of the camp.
Boaz lies down at the end of the heap of grain.
At the end of the conduit of the upper pool.
Not to touch the mountain's edge.

senses.gloss: end of the earth, of the heavens
senses.definition: The farthest reach of the earth or the heavens; “from one end … to the other end” is the whole of it.

evidence.note: “From one end of the heavens to the other end of the heavens”: the whole creation searched.
Gods of peoples “near to you or far from you, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth”.
“Bring my sons from afar, and my daughters from the end of the earth”: the end set beside what is far.
“A nation from afar, from the end of the earth, as the eagle flies”.
Israel scattered “from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth”.
“If your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there Yahweh your God will gather you.”
Nehemiah pleads Deu 30:4.
“That my salvation may be to the end of the earth”; quoted Act 13:47.
The heavens' words “to the end of the world”; quoted Rom 10:18.
The sun goes out “from the end of the heavens”.
Making wars cease to the end of the earth.
“From the end of the earth I call to you.”
The fool's eyes are “at the end of the earth”, far from what is before him.

senses.definition: With מִן, “at the end of” a span of days, months or years.

evidence.note: “At the end of 150 days the waters had decreased.”
“At the end of three days”.
The tithe “at the end of every three years”.
“At the end of seven months” of burying.

senses.gloss: from the end: the whole range; from among
senses.definition: “From the end” of a people or a number is from its whole extent, every part of it, and so “from among” them.

evidence.note: The men of Sodom, “from young to old, all the people from the end”: every part of the city.
Joseph took five men “from among (מִקְצֵה) his brothers”.
“Only its end you will see, and all of it you will not see”: the end set against the whole.
The people take a man “from among them” as watchman.
Babylon taken “from end to end”.
Every man to his gain, “from his end”: every one of them.

senses.definition: אֵין קֵצֶה, “there is no end”: of treasure, chariots, plunder, corpses or allies, past counting.

evidence.note: “No end to his treasures … no end to his chariots.”
“No end to the dead bodies”.

evidence.locator: Deu.4.32, קְצֵה … קְצֵה → ἄκρον … ἄκρου; Deu.30.4 → ἄκρου; Psa.19.7 → ἄκρου; ἄκρον renders קָצֶה ×14

evidence.note: The Son of man's angels gather his chosen “from the ends of the heavens to their ends”: the words of Deu 4:32; 30:4.
“From the end of the earth to the end of heaven”.
Paul and Barnabas quote Isa 49:6: “for salvation to the end (ἐσχάτου) of the earth”.
Witnesses “to the end of the earth”.

evidence.locator: Psa.46.10; Psa.61.3, קְצֵה → περάτων; Nam.2.10; 3.3; 3.9, קֵצֶה → πέρας

evidence.note: Quoting Psa 19:5: “their words to the ends (πέρατα) of the world”.
The queen of the south came “from the ends of the earth”.

parallels.note: The end of the earth is what is far.

phrases.gloss: from one end … to the other end
at the end of three days

words.summary: Mostly plural, קְצוֹת: the two ends of the covering lid, the breastpiece and the cherub's wings, and the ends of the earth.

senses.definition: The two or four ends or corners of a made thing.

evidence.note: Two cherubim “from the two ends of the covering lid”.
Ten cubits “from the ends of its wings to the ends of its wings”.
The vine wood: “its two ends the fire consumes, and its middle is burned”.
Rings on the four corners of the grating.

senses.gloss: ends of the earth, of the heavens
senses.definition: The farthest parts of the earth or the heavens, and those who live there.

evidence.note: Yahweh, “Creator of the ends of the earth”.
“From the ends of the earth … from its far corners (אֲצִילֶיהָ)”.
“The four winds from the four ends of the heavens”.
God looks to the ends of the earth and sees under all the heavens.
“The dwellers of the ends” fear his signs.
The sun's circuit “to their ends”.

senses.definition: The outer edges only, as against the whole.

evidence.note: “These are the edges of his ways, and how small a word we hear of him!”

senses.gloss: from the ends: from the whole range, all sorts
senses.definition: Priests made “from the ends of the people”: from all of it, anyone at all, not from the line Yahweh chose.

evidence.note: Jeroboam's priests “from the ends of the people, who were not of the sons of Levi”.
“Whoever wished, he filled his hand”.
Five men “from their ends”: from their whole number.

words.summary: Six times, five in Daniel and Nehemiah with מִן or לְ (מִקְצָת): “at the end of” a time, and “from the end of”, that is, part or some of. The Aramaic of Daniel has the same word.

senses.definition: The ends or corners of the bronze grating.

evidence.note: Four rings “on the four ends” of the grating.

senses.definition: With מִן or לְ, at the close of a set time.

evidence.note: “At the end of ten days” they looked better.
“At the end of the days” the king had set.
Three years' training, “and at the end of them” to stand before the king.

senses.definition: מִקְצָת, “from the end of”, a part of a whole: some of.

evidence.note: Jehoiakim and “some of the vessels of the house of God”.
“Some of the heads of the fathers” gave to the work.

words.summary: Daniel's Aramaic, three times, as the Hebrew קְצָת of the same book: “at the end of” and, with מִן, “partly”.

senses.definition: לִקְצָת, at the close of a set time.

evidence.note: “At the end of twelve months” Nebuchadnezzar walked on his palace.
“At the end of the days” his reason returned to him.

senses.definition: מִן־קְצָת, part of a whole.

evidence.note: “Part of the kingdom will be strong, and part of it brittle”, as the toes were part iron, part clay.

words.summary: Three times, in the construct plural קַצְוֵי.

senses.gloss: ends of the earth; borders of the land
senses.definition: The farthest parts of the earth, and the outer borders of the land.

evidence.note: God's praise “to the ends of the earth”.
“The confidence of all the ends of the earth and the distant seas”.
Yahweh has added to the nation and “broadened all the borders of the land”.

words.gloss: cut off, cut short; scrape off
words.summary: Five uses, in three stems. Of the twenty tokens under its key, fifteen are the noun קְצוֹת “ends”, filed here by spelling. To cut off is to make an end: Yahweh “began to cut off in Israel” as Hazael struck its borders (2Ki 10:32). Aramaic qṣy, “break (bread)”, and the Peshitta's ܩܨܐ are the same verb.

senses.definition: To cut off peoples, bringing them to an end.

evidence.note: “Cutting off many peoples”, and sinning against your own soul.

senses.definition: To cut off a part, to cut short.

evidence.note: “Yahweh began to cut off in Israel, and Hazael struck them in all the borders of Israel”: the land cut short at its edges.
Sending words by a fool is “cutting off feet”.

senses.definition: To have the plaster of an infected house scraped off.

evidence.note: The house scraped all around, and the dust they scrape off poured out outside the city.
“After the scraping off of the house”.

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܩܨܐ (qṣā), for κλάω: Jesus breaks the bread at the feedings and at the last supper, and the ecclesia breaks it in remembrance.

senses.definition: To break bread to share it.

evidence.note: “Jesus took bread, blessed, and broke it, and gave to his disciples.”
“The bread that we break, is it not the sharing of the body of the Messiah?”
Known to them “in the breaking of bread”.

senses.definition: Of the body of Jesus, given up for his disciples.

evidence.note: “This is my body, which is broken (ܡܬܩܨܐ) for you.”

words.summary: The Peshitta's ܩܨܝܐ (qṣāyā), for κλάσμα “broken piece” and κλάσις “breaking”.

senses.definition: The broken pieces of bread left over at the feedings.

evidence.note: “Gather the broken pieces that are left, that nothing be lost.”

senses.definition: The act of breaking the bread together.

evidence.note: They continued in the apostles' teaching and fellowship, “in the breaking of bread” and prayers.

words.summary: Twelve times: a commander in war and a ruler who should know justice, set beside “head” (רֹאשׁ). Its tie to the root is not clear. Arabic qāḍin “judge”, from qaḍā “decide”, shows ṣ́ behind צ where the “end” words show ṣ, so it may be another older root in the same spelling; the cognate is only possible.

senses.definition: One set over others to lead them in war and to judge them.

evidence.note: “The commanders of the men of war” who went with Joshua.
Gilead asks Jephthah, “Be our commander, that we may fight the sons of Ammon.”
The people made him “head and commander” over them.
“Heads of Jacob and commanders of the house of Israel: is it not for you to know justice?”
The ant has “no commander, officer or ruler”.
“Rulers of Sodom”, of Jerusalem's rulers.
“You have a cloak; be our ruler.”
By patience a commander is persuaded.
A commander puts an end to the king of the north's reproach.

evidence.locator: Jdg.11.6, קָצִין → ἀρχηγόν; ἀρχηγός renders קָצִין ×4

evidence.note: God exalted Jesus “a prince (ἀρχηγόν) and a saviour”.
“The leader (ἀρχηγόν) of their salvation” made complete through sufferings.

cognates.gloss: be far, remote; farthest, farthest part; go to the utmost point
cognates.note: The outermost point, as the Hebrew's end of the earth and edge of a place. Arabic shows ṣ behind צ.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2989, art. قصى, اِسْتَقْصَى (n42695)
evidence.note: “He went to the utmost length, or point … He proceeded to extremities. He was, or became, extreme.”
أَقْصَى “furthest, most distant; farthest part”; قَصِيّ “far, remote”.

cognates.note: The Targums' word, rendering Hebrew קְצֵה in Num 22:41. Aramaic צ shows ṣ (ṣ́ appears there as ע or ק).

evidence.note: “Part. Targ. O. Num. XXII, 41. Targ. Job IV, 12 … 1) extreme end. Targ. Y. Num. l. c.”

cognates.note: Galilean and Palestinian Jewish Aramaic and Syriac, “break bread”; Babylonian, “set aside”. The cutting off of the Hebrew verb.

evidence.locator: qṣy vb., G sense 1 “to break (as bread)”; C “to set aside”; Gt “to be broken”
evidence.note: PT Ber 10a: “when he would break (qṣy) bread”; BT Yom 17a, the cell “was set aside”.

evidence.locator: lexeme 2863, QCA (root QCA), break; lexeme 2864, QCYA, fragment

cognates.note: Would make קָצִין “one who decides”, fitting rulers who should “know justice” (Mic 3:1). Arabic ḍ shows ṣ́ behind צ, against the ṣ of the “end” cognates, so קָצִין would be a second older root in this spelling.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 2989, art. قضى, قَضَى (n42704)
evidence.note: “He finished a thing entirely, by word, or by deed. This is the primary meaning … He decided judicially, or judged.”
qāḍin “judge”.

doctrine.statement: Moses warned that Yahweh would scatter Israel “among all the peoples, from one end of the earth to the other end of the earth” (Deu 28:64), by a nation brought “from the end of the earth” (Deu 28:49). He promised in the same words: “If your outcasts are at the end of the heavens, from there Yahweh your God will gather you … and bring you into the land which your fathers possessed, and you will possess it” (Deu 30:4–5). Nehemiah pleaded that promise (Neh 1:9), and Isaiah has Yahweh say to north and south, “bring my sons from afar and my daughters from the end of the earth” (Isa 43:6). Jesus takes up the words of Deu 30:4 for his coming: the Son of man sends his angels to gather his chosen “from one end of the heavens to the other” (Mat 24:31; Mrk 13:27). The scattering was to the literal ends of the earth, and the gathering out of them is to the land the fathers possessed, at the coming of the Son of man.

Yahweh tells his servant that raising up Jacob's tribes is too small a thing: “I have given you as a light of the nations, that my salvation may be to the end of the earth” (Isa 49:6). Paul and Barnabas quote it as the command for turning to the gentiles (Act 13:47), as Jesus sent his witnesses “to the end of the earth” (Act 1:8). Paul hears in Psa 19:5, the heavens' words going “to the end of the world”, the preaching that has gone out (Rom 10:18). Yahweh has made it heard to the end of the earth, “Say to the daughter of Zion, Behold, your salvation comes” (Isa 62:11). From the verses: the salvation of Israel's God was always meant for the ends of the earth, and it reaches them through the servant and those he sends.

note: BDB keys: s.co.ad (קֵצֶה) lists the same 97 tokens as s.co.ab, so only s.co.ab is named; the קֵצֶה spelling (Isa 2:7; Nam 2:10; 3:3, 9) is folded into קָצֶה. s.co.aa (verb) shares 15 קְצוֹת tokens with the noun s.co.ac; Hab 2:10 is the verb. m.df.bb (מִקְצָת) and s.cx.ad are zero-token cross-references, not named. Psa 65:9 קְצָוֺת is aligned as קְצָת by MACULA but filed under s.co.ac. Jos 19:13 עֵת קָצִין (Eth-kazin) is a place in TIPNR (Eth-kazin@Jos.19.13), counted under s.cp.ab, not cited; no personal names from the root. In word_info, Dan 4:11 Aramaic וְקַצִּצוּ is rooted קצא; it belongs to קצץ. Open questions: (1) whether קָצִין is of this root (ṣ) or a second root behind ṣ́ (Arabic qāḍī); Arabic قضى “finish entirely; انقضى came to an end, was cut off” also resembles “end” and “cut off”, but Aramaic qṣy and qṣt keep צ, which points to ṣ for those. (2) The relation to קצץ “cut off” and קֵץ “end” (biconsonantal qṣ), which have no entry yet. Leads not followed: Phoenician קצ “cut off” (Krahmalkov), Ugaritic, Ge'ez. Mishnaic Hebrew hiphil הִקְצָה “set aside” matches Babylonian Aramaic aphel “set aside” (CAL).
